userQuestion: How can I navigate the transition after leaving my hometown?
reflectionsText: Part of me is nostalgic while another part is ready for reinvention.
excerpt: If things keep moving as they are, the trajectory leans toward The Star. A figure kneels under a large star, pouring one pitcher into a pool and the other onto the land. That image speaks almost directly to your reflection. One hand tends the emotional reservoir of memory and the people back home, and the other waters new ground. Neither pitcher gets dropped. The figure is also unadorned, which suggests the reinvention ahead may be quieter than a dramatic makeover. It's less "new me" and more "me, without the parts I was only holding up for others."
